lines: Hong Kong flattened two islands to build one airport.
The old airport, Kai Tak, sat in the middle of the city, with one runway sticking into the harbor.
By the 1990s, one in three flights was delayed.
So engineers flattened two small islands, and reclaimed more than 9 square kilometers from the sea.
Construction started in 1991. The new airport opened in July 1998.
